claim: Kandyan resilience and legitimacy repeatedly depended on selective incorporation of external people, lineages and religious networks—from Portuguese-linked exiles and Nayaka courts to Ayutthaya ordination—rather than on cultural isolation.
bounded_by: This is a bounded synthesis of recurring adaptation, not a claim that every foreign connection was accepted, equivalent or politically successful.
notes: Corrects the sealed-mountain-kingdom image without weakening the separately sourced role of defensive geography.
